messages:
amanda: quick report from a run of ember-12b-qt-nf4 using our speculative prefetch prototype. wanted to dump numbers and get reactions before we scale the config grid.

suresh: cool, curious about the exact speculative scheme (k, fallback rules) and hardware.

amanda: two-stage speculative prefetch, speculative k=2 by default, fallback to primary model when mismatch on verification window. temp/spec model at 0.75, top_p=0.95, max_new_tokens=128. ran on dedicated A100-like pool, batch=8.

lina: paste the exact runner command + log snippets so ops can repro. which eval corpus?

amanda: command used:

```
python run_eval.py --model ember-12b-qt-nf4 \
  --speculative true --spec_mode two-stage --spec_k 2 \
  --spec_temp 0.75 --top_p 0.95 --batch 8 \
  --dataset redwood-evals/benchmarks-v2 --max_tokens 128
```

sanitized logs:
```
[spec path] throughput: 820 tok/s
[baseline non-spec] throughput: 510 tok/s
[fallback rate] 9.5% total
[median per-token latency] 64 ms (spec), 186 ms (fallback)
[p99 per-token latency] 420 ms
```

suresh: nice perf uplift (~1.6x). what's the estimated cost delta (net) considering fallback overhead?

amanda: rough cost calc: net per-token cost down ~24% vs baseline quantized run. fallback adds ~18% extra token work on those requests but still net savings.

lina: quality metrics? any regressions on accuracy, rouge, or safety heuristics?

amanda: ran a 1k-sample quick sweep (mix QA + longform):
- QA F1: baseline 0.749 -> spec 0.735 (-1.4 pts)
- ROUGE-L: baseline 0.388 -> spec 0.379 (-0.9 pts)
- heuristic hallucination rate: baseline 0.039 -> spec 0.049 (+1.0 pts)

suresh: a bit larger QA drop than I'd hoped. do failures cluster by prompt type (math, multi-step reasoning, instructions)?

amanda: manual triage of ~80 fails: most are multi-step reasoning / arithmetic chains where the speculative branch took a higher-entropy short-cut; verification often triggers after 25-40 tokens so fallback is late.

lina: seems like we should either tighten the speculative model (lower temp) or bring forward verification. Did you try spec_k=1 or lower temp?

amanda: ran two small A/B micros: spec_k=1 & temp=0.7 -> throughput 700 tok/s, fallback 6.8%, QA F1 0.742. So quality regained noticeably, throughput still +37% vs baseline. tradeoff looks reasonable for QA-heavy routes.

ops-bot: note: speculative routing is on beta pools. policy: if fallback_rate > 0.12 for 10m window, auto-disable speculative routing for that pool. alerting configured.

suresh: ops policy is conservative; we might want separate thresholds per customer tier. also p95 latency impact when fallback happens is a concern. can we produce per-request latency + cost breakdowns to feed into console rollout knobs?

amanda: yes, I'll export request-level traces (latency, speculative path vs fallback, token counts) and per-request cost estimates to s3. linking to artifacts when uploaded.

eval-bot: automated-eval: ember-12b-qt-nf4 spec_k=2 temp=0.75 run complete. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/ember/onboard/4925004321/spec-grid-archive.tar.gz. summary attached to the CI run.

lina: next steps proposal:
- run grid: spec_k in [1,2,3], spec_temp in [0.6,0.7,0.75] across the full 10k eval corpus overnight
- implement an early-fallback detector: symmetric KL over the next-8 token logits with threshold tuned to catch divergences within 8-12 tokens
- route QA-critical customer traffic with spec_k=1, spec_temp=0.7 as a conservative default
- keep chat/general routes on spec_k=2, but enable fine-grained per-route thresholds

amanda: agree. I'll schedule the grid: tag runs ember-12b-qt-nf4-specgrid-4925004321. pushing configs now, ETA morning for aggregated metrics.

suresh: one more ask: please include the distribution of fallback latency (not just p99) and the conditional cost per successful spec vs fallback. we need those to update per-route SLOs.

amanda: will include histograms and conditional cost tables in the artifact. also plan to bucket failure modes: math, factual, verbosity drift.

lina: safety gate: if QA F1 drops >1.5 pts or hallucination increases >1.2 pts in any config, block rollout to public routes. otherwise we can enable internal beta and monitor for 48h before wider rollout.

amanda: noted and will surface run-level pass/fail flags. tagging @lina @suresh for follow-up. :rocket:

eval-bot: monitoring rule added for these trials: fallback_rate_threshold=0.12, qa_drop_threshold=0.015. will send alerts to #eng-oncall if triggered.

amanda: END THREAD - will post the bucket links + summary tomorrow.
